title: FCC Chairman says there is ‘common ground’ on ending illegal discrimination, DEI
summary: In May, 18 members of Congress sent a letter questioning the agency’s targeting of companies’ DEI policies.

title: AI may miss hidden talent. Recruiters can take steps to prevent that from happening.
summary: Employers must design AI systems that recognize nontraditional job candidates’ experience and credentials, a SHRM26 speaker said.

title: DEI’s next era? Reorientation, says SHRM’s Johnny Taylor Jr.
summary: In conversation with HR Dive, SHRM’s president and CEO forecasted the future of DEI in 2027 and 2028.

title: Younger workers may be falling behind in critical thinking skills
summary: The three largest skill gaps in the younger workforce represent “the very skills most essential to humans in the AI era,” per a report from Cangrade.

title: Monster’s parent company rebuffs competitor’s ‘deficient’ antitrust lawsuit
summary: Bold Limited said Rocket Resume’s lawsuit alleging that it monopolized the market for resume-building platforms “fails at every step.”

title: Workday can’t shake California AI discrimination claims
summary: Because Workday is headquartered in California, a “sufficient nexus” exists to apply the state law even to nonresidents, a federal judge determined.

title: 7 stories on new and recent grads in the labor market
summary: Generation Z interns are increasingly citing old-school, hands-on experiences as among the most valuable workplace exposures they can have.

title: EEOC opens antisemitism probe into NEA, Brandeis Center says
summary: The center’s complaint alleges the teachers union didn’t specify Jews as the primary victims of the Holocaust, among other things.

title: Onboarding begins even before a candidate’s first interview, one HR pro says
summary: Lindsay Gainor, a vice president of HR at ServiceMaster Brands, shares onboarding tips to help ensure new hires stay past the one-year mark.

title: Remote workers represent ‘a disproportionate share’ of unemployed adults, Gallup says
summary: While artificial intelligence wasn’t cited as the reason for layoffs, its impact was often evident in more subtle ways, the report noted.
